question: Do six inert query/no-op probes on uncovered socket/fcntl/mmap/dup2 boundaries — a lone AF_UNIX SOCK_STREAM socket, getsockopt SO_ERROR and SO_ACCEPTCONN, fcntl F_GETSIG, mmap MAP_NORESERVE, and the POSIX dup2(fd,fd) no-op — reach L2 parity across the golden ptrace backend and the e9patch-rewritten ptrace path?

environment.note: Fleet PMU heavily contended during vetting (loadavg ~67-140, dozens of concurrent --verify). These probes have minimal RCBs and hit L2 for both golden and e9. Vetting used a killpg-on-wedge retry harness (compat-envelope/collect-e9patch-compat.rs) for the verify legs; a concurrent full corpus run also reported all six new guests PASS_L2 (sites c/1 m/1 b0/0, prologue=8, tail_match=yes). Any non-pass among the 227 PRE-EXISTING guests in a contended full run is a transient PMU verify-wedge, not a regression from this additive change (round 34 was 227/227 clean at the base SHA).

result.golden_ptrace: 6/6 L2 Determinism verified; native==golden and expected stdout matched
result.e9patch: 6/6 PASS_L2 exit=0 sites c/1 m/1 b0/0 prologue=8 tail_match=yes; scorecard collector: every ptrace arm det=1, every e9patch arm det=1 par=1
result.full_corpus_run: clean re-run 233/233 PASS_L2 (0 non-passes). A first, more heavily contended run reported 228/233 with all 6 new guests passing; the 5 non-passes were pre-existing guests transiently wedged on the verify leg under PMU load and all passed on the immediate clean re-run, confirming env artifacts not regressions (see environment note)
